nodes.sectionHeader: PLAINTIFF WAS INDUCED TO LEAVE PRIOR EMPLOYMENT
nodes.content:
{{para}}. The Plaintiff was actively recruited by the Defendant from {{pronoun_possessive}} position with {{prior_employer}}, where {{pronoun_subject}} had been continuously employed for approximately {{prior_service}} years in a secure role.

{{para}}. The Defendant, through {{recruiter_name_and_title}}, approached the Plaintiff and made representations regarding {{inducement_representations}} in order to persuade the Plaintiff to leave {{pronoun_possessive}} prior employment and accept the Defendant's offer.

{{para}}. Relying on the Defendant's representations, the Plaintiff resigned from {{pronoun_possessive}} position with {{prior_employer}} and accepted the Defendant's offer of employment. The Plaintiff would not have done so absent those representations.

{{para}}. The Plaintiff pleads that {{pronoun_possessive}} inducement from secure, long-term employment is a significant factor in the assessment of reasonable notice, and that {{pronoun_possessive}} {{prior_service}} years of accumulated service with {{prior_employer}} must be taken into account. The Defendant received the full benefit of the experience, institutional knowledge, and professional standing the Plaintiff developed during those years and cannot treat the Plaintiff as a new entrant to the workforce for the purposes of assessing notice.

{{#if promises_not_fulfilled}}
{{para}}. The representations made to the Plaintiff during the recruitment process were inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading. The Plaintiff pleads the particulars of those misrepresentations in the section below.
{{/if}}
nodes.notes: All paragraphs always fire when block triggered except final bridge paragraph which fires conditionally when promises_not_fulfilled = YES.

nodes.content:
{{para}}. The Plaintiff pleads that the Defendant is liable for negligent misrepresentation in connection with the representations made during the recruitment process.

{{para}}. During the recruitment process, the Defendant represented to the Plaintiff that {{misrepresentation_subject}}. Those representations were inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading in the circumstances in which they were made.

{{para}}. The Defendant owed the Plaintiff a duty of care in making those representations. The Plaintiff was a known and identifiable individual who would foreseeably rely on the Defendant's representations in deciding whether to accept the offer of employment and resign from {{pronoun_possessive}} prior position.

{{para}}. The Plaintiff reasonably relied on the Defendant's representations. In reliance on those representations, the Plaintiff resigned from {{pronoun_possessive}} secure position with {{prior_employer}}, where {{pronoun_subject}} had accumulated {{prior_service}} years of service, and accepted the Defendant's offer.

{{para}}. The representations were false. Had the Plaintiff known the true state of affairs, {{pronoun_subject}} would not have resigned from {{pronoun_possessive}} prior position or accepted the Defendant's offer.

{{para}}. As a result of the Defendant's negligent misrepresentations, the Plaintiff suffered loss. The Plaintiff's damages are assessed on a reliance basis and are not limited by or subsumed within the notice period damages claimed above. The Plaintiff claims the difference between the compensation actually received from the Defendant and the compensation that would have been received had the representations been accurate, whether by remaining at {{prior_employer}} or by accepting a bona fide alternative opportunity that was available at the time. Full particulars of this calculation will be provided before trial.

{{#if promises_known_false}}
{{para}}. In the further alternative, the Plaintiff pleads that the misrepresentations were made fraudulently, in that the persons who made them knew, or were reckless as to whether, those representations were false at the time they were made. The Plaintiff pleads fraudulent misrepresentation as an alternative basis for the reliance damages claimed above, and further claims punitive damages on the basis of the Defendant's fraudulent conduct.
{{/if}}
nodes.notes: All paragraphs always fire when block triggered except fraudulent misrepresentation paragraph which is conditional and requires mandatory lawyer confirmation before firing.

nodes.sectionHeader: PLAINTIFF WAS EMPLOYED BY COMMON AND RELATED EMPLOYERS
nodes.notes: Opening, documentation, control, and closing paragraphs always fire. Sub-paragraphs (b)(c)(d) conditional. Assembly engine flags if common_employer=YES but only one defendant named in parties section.

nodes.content:
{{para}}. The Plaintiff pleads that following the termination of {{pronoun_possessive}} employment, the Defendant, or persons acting on its behalf, made statements to {{defamation_recipients}} regarding the reasons for the Plaintiff's departure and {{pronoun_possessive}} conduct during employment.

{{para}}. Those statements were false. The true circumstances of the Plaintiff's departure were as follows: {{defamation_true_circumstances}}. The Defendant knew or ought to have known that the statements were false at the time they were made.

{{para}}. The statements were made to individuals in the Plaintiff's professional community and have damaged the Plaintiff's professional reputation. As a result of the Defendant's statements, the Plaintiff has suffered injury to {{pronoun_possessive}} reputation, has experienced difficulty obtaining comparable employment, and has suffered loss and damage.

{{#if defamation_malicious}}
{{para}}. The Plaintiff further pleads that the statements were made maliciously, with knowledge of their falsity or with reckless disregard for their truth, and that the Defendant's conduct warrants an award of aggravated and punitive damages in addition to general damages for defamation.
{{/if}}

{{para}}. The Plaintiff claims general damages for defamation, aggravated damages where the conduct warrants, and special damages for any quantifiable loss resulting from the Defendant's statements, the full particulars of which will be provided before trial.
nodes.notes: All paragraphs always fire when block triggered except malicious conduct paragraph which is conditional. defamation_recipients and defamation_true_circumstances are mandatory lawyer-completion fields.
nodes.newPlaceholders: [DEFAMATION_RECIPIENTS][DEFAMATION_TRUE_CIRCUMSTANCES] = mandatory lawyer-completion; [DEFAMATION_MALICIOUS] = intake or lawyer flag

nodes.content:
{{para}}. The Plaintiff's employment agreement contains a provision purporting to restrict {{pronoun_possessive}} post-employment activities (the "Restrictive Covenant").

{{para}}. The Plaintiff pleads that the Restrictive Covenant is void and unenforceable. {{#if noncompete_post_oct2021}}{{#unless is_executive_noncompete}}The Restrictive Covenant was entered into on {{contract_date}} and is prohibited by section 67.2(1) of the Employment Standards Act, 2000, S.O. 2000, c. 41.{{/unless}}{{/if}}{{#if noncompete_common_law}}The Restrictive Covenant is unreasonable in its scope, duration, and the activities it purports to restrict, and does not protect any legitimate proprietary interest of the Defendant.{{/if}}

{{para}}. The Defendant has {{#if covenant_enforcement_threat}}threatened to enforce{{else}}purported to rely on{{/if}} the Restrictive Covenant following the termination of the Plaintiff's employment. The Plaintiff is not bound by the Restrictive Covenant and intends to pursue comparable employment without restriction.

{{para}}. The Plaintiff claims a declaration that the Restrictive Covenant is void and unenforceable, damages for any loss caused by the Defendant's conduct, and an injunction restraining the Defendant from taking any steps to enforce the Restrictive Covenant.
nodes.notes: All paragraphs fire when block triggered. Unenforceability ground switches between statutory and common law based on contract date and executive flag.

nodes.content:
{{para}}. The Plaintiff pleads that the Defendant intentionally or recklessly intruded upon {{pronoun_possessive}} private affairs without lawful justification.

{{para}}. Specifically, the Defendant {{privacy_breach_description}}. This conduct constituted an invasion of the Plaintiff's private affairs and concerns.

{{para}}. A reasonable person in the Plaintiff's position would regard the Defendant's conduct as highly offensive and as causing distress, humiliation, and anguish.

{{para}}. As a result of the Defendant's conduct, the Plaintiff suffered injury. The Plaintiff claims general damages for intrusion upon seclusion in an amount to be determined by this Honourable Court.
nodes.notes: All paragraphs always fire when block triggered. privacy_breach_description is mandatory lawyer-completion. Assembly engine flags: damages capped at $20,000 per Jones v. Tsige — shown as lawyer advisory note only, not in pleading.

nodes.content:
{{para}}. The Plaintiff pleads that the Defendant is liable for the intentional infliction of mental suffering.

{{para}}. The Defendant engaged in the following conduct toward the Plaintiff: {{iims_conduct_description}}. This conduct was flagrant and outrageous.

{{para}}. The Defendant's conduct was calculated to produce harm to the Plaintiff. The Defendant knew or ought to have known that the conduct would cause the Plaintiff to suffer mental distress.

{{para}}. As a direct result of the Defendant's conduct, the Plaintiff suffered {{iims_illness_description}}, which constitutes a visible and provable illness. The Plaintiff's condition was caused by and is attributable to the Defendant's conduct.

{{para}}. The Plaintiff claims general and special damages for the intentional infliction of mental suffering in an amount to be determined by this Honourable Court.
nodes.notes: All paragraphs always fire when block triggered. Both fields are mandatory lawyer-completion. Assembly engine flags: IIMS requires flagrant conduct calculated to produce harm AND visible provable illness — confirm medical evidence available before pleading.

nodes.content:
{{para}}. The Plaintiff pleads that the Defendant has been unjustly enriched at the Plaintiff's expense.

{{para}}. The Defendant was enriched by reason of the following: {{unjust_enrichment_benefit}}. The Plaintiff was correspondingly deprived of the value of that benefit.

{{para}}. There is no juristic reason for the Defendant's enrichment. The benefit conferred by the Plaintiff was not covered by the terms of the employment agreement, was not gratuitous, and was not the subject of any other legal obligation that would justify the Defendant's retention of it without compensation.

{{para}}. The Plaintiff claims restitution of the value of the benefit conferred on the Defendant, in an amount to be determined by this Honourable Court.
nodes.notes: All paragraphs always fire when block triggered. Assembly engine flags: unusual employee cause — confirm benefit falls outside employment agreement scope before pleading.
